reading.body:
The TierPoint Charlotte Data Center publishes 20,000 square feet of technical space and no IT load figure in megawatts. Without a published power number, no translation into racks or accelerators is possible. The campus sits in Mecklenburg County, North Carolina, and its scale relative to the AI infrastructure this site tracks cannot be assessed from the available data.

The six certifications on record each qualify the campus for a specific class of regulated workload. SOC 1 Type 2 covers financial controls auditing. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment card data. HIPAA and HITRUST together qualify it for protected health information. ISO 27001 certifies an information security management system. ITAR qualifies it for controlled defense and export-restricted technical data. The combination makes this a compliance-oriented facility capable of hosting work that many hyperscale-only campuses cannot accept.

North Carolina has 19 facilities mapped on this site, of which only one has published a megawatt figure. That single figure is 40 MW. This campus ranks second by published megawatts in the state, which reflects the near-total absence of published power data across the state rather than a confirmed size advantage. Whether this campus matters to AI scaling depends on its power capacity, which is not published.
